waves.rationale: No dependencies. #29 is the auth spine; #30 is back-office docs. Parallel.
All depend only on #29 and are independent of each other. Parallel.
Needs tenant context (#32) to know which team the user is admin of.
#35 needs the authz seam (#34); #36 needs the login UI (#31). Parallel.
#37 needs login (#31) + invite generation (#35). #38 needs #35 and effectively the #37 accept path to reject against.

notes: #38 declares 'Blocked by: #35' but its acceptance criteria reject tokens at accept time and reference the #35/#37 path — sequence #38 after #37, not merely after #35.

items.description: End-to-end backend magic-link login loop: new auth.ws Wirespec contract (request/verify/logout/me), single-use hashed tokens with ~15min TTL in the public schema, Spring Session + Redis, EmailSender port with dev/console + test-fake adapters, UserContext from session with a test-profile-only X-User-Id shim.
steps: auth.ws Wirespec contract for the 4 endpoints; run make wirespec.
Flyway V002 (public): magic_link_tokens table — hashed token, email, expiry, used_at.
EmailSender port + no-op/console dev adapter + test fake.
request use case → 202 always, emits token via port.
verify use case → resolve-or-create user, single-use + TTL check, establish session.
logout + GET /api/auth/me.
Enable spring.session.store-type=redis; populate UserContext from session.
Test-profile-only X-User-Id shim to keep existing tests green.
Integration tests (Testcontainers + fake sender).
verify: auth.ws defines the four endpoints; Kotlin generated via make wirespec (generated files not hand-edited).
Flyway V002 adds magic_link_tokens (hashed, email-bound, TTL, used_at); baseline V001 not edited.
request returns 202 regardless of account existence; fake EmailSender captures the emitted link/token.
verify(valid token) establishes a session; subsequent GET /api/auth/me over the same cookie returns the user.
verify(expired or already-used token) is rejected.
logout clears the session; GET /api/auth/me afterwards is unauthenticated.
spring.session.store-type=redis enabled for prod; sessions backed by Redis.
UserContext populated from the session; test-profile-only header shim keeps controller integration tests working.
completedSteps: auth.ws Wirespec contract for the 4 endpoints; run make wirespec.
Flyway V003 (public): magic_link_tokens table — hashed token, email, expiry, used_at. (V002 was already taken by seed data, so V003 used instead)
EmailSender port + no-op/console dev adapter + test fake.
request use case → 202 always, emits token via port.
verify use case → resolve-or-create user, single-use + TTL check, establish session.

items.description: Documented back-office procedure for the owner to provision a Team and seed its membership/roles, since self-service team creation is out of scope for v1 (ADR-0001, ADR-0008, ADR-0009).
steps: Document teams row + tenant-schema provisioning.
Document owner-as-admin team_member seeding.
Document one-role-per-member seeding (ADR-0009); link ADR-0001/0008.
Dry-run the procedure locally; confirm a seeded member can later log in.
verify: A documented procedure (e.g. under docs/) describes provisioning a team end-to-end: teams row, tenant schema, owner as admin team_member, one role per member.
The procedure is runnable as written against local/dev and yields a team whose members can subsequently log in.
Uses CONTEXT.md vocabulary (Team, Member, Role, Admin) and references ADR-0001/0008/0009.
No self-service team-creation UI or endpoint is introduced.

items.description: Frontend magic-link login experience (FSD): login screen, magic-link landing route, logout, user store hydrated from /api/auth/me (replacing the dev X-User-Id store), expired/used-link messaging, and MSW dev handlers.
steps: Consume the generated Wirespec TS client for auth.
Login screen: email → request → 'check your email'.
Magic-link landing route → verify → redirect.
User store hydrated from /api/auth/me (retire X-User-Id store).
Logout action; expired/used link error state.
MSW handlers for request/verify/logout/me.
verify: Login screen submits email and shows a 'check your email' confirmation; reveals nothing about account existence.
Magic-link landing route verifies the token and redirects an authenticated user into the app.
Current user is sourced from GET /api/auth/me; the dev X-User-Id store no longer drives identity.
Logout clears the session and returns to login.
Expired/used link renders a clear, actionable error prompting a fresh link.
MSW handlers cover request/verify/logout/me.
Generated Wirespec TS client consumed (not hand-edited); FSD layer boundaries respected.

items.description: Resolve TenantContext from the authenticated session user's team_members row instead of trusting X-Team-Id. v1 assumes one team per user; multi-team switching deferred. Keep a test-profile-only shim.
steps: Resolve TenantContext from the session user's team_members row.
Stop trusting X-Team-Id in prod; keep test-profile shim.
Handle 'user with no team' cleanly (no silent fallback).
Integration test for both paths.
verify: In prod, TenantContext resolved from the session user's team_members row (one-team-per-user assumption documented).
X-Team-Id no longer trusted in prod; test-profile-only shim remains.
A logged-in member's requests resolve to their tenant schema with no client-supplied team id.
Integration test: session user with a team_members row reaches their tenant schema; a user with no team handled cleanly.

items.description: Record changed-by actor on Attendance (ADR-0003, stories 11–12). Domain Attendance gains changedBy, set from UserContext on every write, including cross-member edits. Trust-based editing preserved; actor always recorded for a future permission/audit layer.
steps: Tenant Flyway V002: add changed_by (UUID) to attendances.
Domain Attendance.changedBy + JPA entity/mapper.
setAttendance reads actor from UserContext.
Integration test incl. cross-member edit.
verify: Tenant V002 adds changed_by (UUID) to attendances; baseline tenant migration not edited.
Domain Attendance carries changedBy; JPA entity/mapper persist it.
setAttendance sets changedBy from the session UserContext.
Editing another member's attendance records the editor as changedBy, not the owner.
Integration test over HTTP asserts changedBy = session user, including the cross-member case.

items.description: Reusable authorization seam gating admin-only actions on teamRole == admin (from team_members in the resolved team context), applied to Event CRUD. Frontend hides admin-only controls from non-admins.
steps: Reusable 'is admin of resolved team' check (from team_members).
Apply to Event create/update/delete → 403 for non-admin.
Frontend hides admin event controls.
Integration test: non-admin 403 / admin success.
verify: A reusable check resolves whether the current session user is an Admin of the resolved team.
Event create/update/delete reject a non-admin session with 403; an admin session succeeds.
Frontend hides event admin controls for non-admins.
Integration test: non-admin → 403 on event CRUD; admin → success.

items.description: Admin generates a single shareable invite link bound to their team. POST /api/invitations (admin-gated via #34) returns a reusable token in the platform invitations schema. Admin UI generates and copies the link.
steps: Wirespec POST /api/invitations; Flyway public invitations table (token bound to team).
Use case (admin-gated via #34) returns reusable link.
Admin UI: generate + copy.
Integration test: admin creates / non-admin 403.
verify: POST /api/invitations returns the invite link for the admin's team.
Endpoint gated admin-only via the #34 seam; non-admin → 403.
Invite token bound to the team in the platform invitations schema (one link, reusable by many joiners).
Frontend admin control generates the link and lets the admin copy it.
Integration test: admin creates an invite; non-admin rejected.

items.description: Auth guard on app routes (TanStack Router): unauthenticated visitors redirect to login; the store hydrates from /api/auth/me on load so a valid persisted session skips login; authenticated members land in their team's events.
steps: TanStack Router guard → redirect unauthenticated to login.
Hydrate user from /api/auth/me on load (valid session skips login).
Post-login lands in team events; logout blocks protected routes.
verify: Visiting a protected route while unauthenticated redirects to login.
On load, the app hydrates current-user from GET /api/auth/me; a valid session skips login.
After login, the member lands in their team's events.
Logout returns to login and protected routes are no longer reachable.

items.description: Invite acceptance & member onboarding (stories 9, 10). Invite-link landing route collects email → drives magic-link auth; POST /api/invitations/{token}/accept adds the authenticated user as a team_member and provisions tenant membership. New member lands in team events.
steps: Invite landing route: token → collect email → drive magic-link auth.
POST /api/invitations/{token}/accept → add team_member + provision tenant membership.
Reject invalid/unknown token.
New member lands in team events.
Integration test: accept → becomes team_member.
verify: Invite landing route accepts a token, collects email, and drives the magic-link auth flow.
POST /api/invitations/{token}/accept adds the authenticated user as a team_member of the invited team and provisions tenant membership.
A freshly onboarded member lands in the team's events.
Accepting with an invalid/unknown invite token is rejected cleanly.
Integration test: invite accept → the authenticated user becomes a team_member of the invited team.

items.description: Admin can rotate or expire the invite link to stop new joins (story 8). Rotating issues a fresh token and invalidates the previous one; expired/rotated tokens are rejected at accept time. Admin-only via the #34 seam.
steps: Rotate (new token, invalidate old) + expire endpoint, admin-gated.
Accept path rejects rotated/expired tokens.
Admin UI rotate/expire + show active link.
Integration test: rotate → old rejected/new accepted; expire → rejected.
verify: An admin can rotate the invite link (new token issued, previous invalidated) and/or expire it.
Accepting via a rotated/expired invite token is rejected (ties into the #35/#37 accept path).
Endpoint gated admin-only; non-admin → 403.
Frontend admin control exposes rotate/expire and surfaces the current active link.
Integration test: rotate → old token rejected, new accepted; expire → token rejected.
